claims: The second crew member from the U.S. F-15E strike eagle shot down over Iran was rescued safe and sound early Sunday, April 5, 2026, according to President Trump and U.S. officials.
The second crew member from the U.S. F-15E strike eagle shot down over Iran was rescued following a "daring operation" after being missing for two days, officials said.
The F-15E jet was shot down over Iran on Friday, April 3, 2026.
One crew member from the F-15E jet was rescued shortly after it was shot down.
The second crew member from the F-15E jet remained missing for two days.
The second crew member from the F-15E jet was found in a remote area of Iran after an intensive search-and-rescue effort.
Reports indicate a "heavy firefight" occurred during the rescue of the second crew member from the F-15E jet.
A U.S. A-10 Warthog attack plane crashed near the Strait of Hormuz during the same period.
The pilot from the U.S. A-10 Warthog attack plane was safely rescued.
Both airmen from the initial F-15E incident are safe.
